name: Executive order of August 25, 1877 restoring the Hot Springs (Ojo Caliente) reservation to the public domain
nations: Chiricahua and Warm Springs (Chihene) Apache, today the Fort Sill Apache Tribe and Chiricahua descendants at Mescalero
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. It restored to the public domain the Hot Springs reservation as established by the executive order of December 21, 1875 (Royce p. 890, area 587).
landTaken: The Hot Springs reservation of December 21, 1875 (Royce area 587). No acreage was found in a source opened.
compensation: None for this order. The Chiricahua aboriginal land claim (Dockets 30-A and 48-A) ended in a 1971 judgment entered on a stipulation; see cession-1876-10-30-apache.
today: The Indian Claims Commission found that in 1876-1877 the Government reversed its policy of settling the Chiricahua on reservations in their homelands, abolished the Ojo Caliente reservation on August 25, 1877 and moved them toward San Carlos; it dated the taking of their aboriginal title to September 4, 1886, Geronimo's surrender (findings 14(a) and 14(b)). That is a finding about aboriginal title, not about this order.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says its original territory covered much of the Southwest, including eastern Arizona and western New Mexico, that its people endured nearly a decade of imprisonment and exile in Florida and Alabama before being moved to Oklahoma in 1894, and that a reservation proclamation for its New Mexico land was issued in November 2011.

openQuestions: An executive order taking back executive-order land is not a breach by itself (Jordan, 2026-11-08). The Commission names this abolition in finding 14(b) but dates the taking to September 4, 1886, so the file keeps no-breach-found, consistent with cession-1875-12-21-southern-apache and cession-1874-11-24-apache-southern. Jordan may want to rule on whether a finding that names the abolition counts for its row.
This record maps the same polygon (area 587) as cession-1875-12-21-southern-apache, which made the reservation; this one ended it. Different events, so no sameEventAs.
treaties.json error: presentDayTribes is empty for this record; the Fort Sill Apache Tribe should be listed. Not edited.

Audit 2026-11-08: OSU 2269 reopened: findings 14(a) and 14(b) say the Ojo Caliente reservation was abolished on August 25, 1877 and the taking was September 4, 1886, as recorded. Court of Claims index for Apache lists only ICC appeals (Fort Sill Apache 1973). no-breach-found confirmed under Jordan's rule; not the same event as cession-1874-04-09-southern-apache (area 588 vs 587), so no sameEventAs.
